questions.article: Terrorism in the Light of Islamic Teachings
questions.q: How does the author define terrorism?
options: Armed struggle by non-governmental actors
Yes. Individuals and groups may work only by peaceful means.
Any use of force by anyone
Not quite. The article says: Armed struggle by non-governmental actors.
Violence that crosses national borders
Not quite. The article says: Armed struggle by non-governmental actors.
War declared without warning
Not quite. The article says: Armed struggle by non-governmental actors.
questions.rationale: “My definition of terrorism is that, it is an armed struggle by non-governmental actors… only an established government has the right to use arms.”

questions.article: Terrorism in the Light of Islamic Teachings
questions.q: The article compares a surgeon who cuts the wrong part with a person who is not a doctor using a knife. What distinction does this explain?
options: Intention matters more than the act
Not quite. The article says: A state that uses violence wrongly misuses a right it has; a non-state group has no such right at all.
Trained fighters cause less harm than untrained ones
Not quite. The article says: A state that uses violence wrongly misuses a right it has; a non-state group has no such right at all.
A state that uses violence wrongly misuses a right it has; a non-state group has no such right at all
Well reasoned. Both can be at fault, but in different ways.
Doctors, like rulers, are above the law
Not quite. The article says: A state that uses violence wrongly misuses a right it has; a non-state group has no such right at all.
questions.rationale: “There is a distinction between doing something which one has no right to, on the one hand, and misusing a right that one is legally entitled to.”

questions.q: What does the forbidden tree stand for in the article’s reading of the story of Adam and Eve?
options: The company of other people
Not quite. The article says: The wrongs that man, though free, must keep away from.
The wrongs that man, though free, must keep away from
Correct. Conscience is the guide that tells right from wrong.
The wealth of this world
Not quite. The article says: The wrongs that man, though free, must keep away from.
Knowledge that is hidden from man
Not quite. The article says: The wrongs that man, though free, must keep away from.
questions.rationale: “Man was created as a free creature… The condition was that he should refrain from wrongdoing. The forbidden tree of paradise was a symbol of ‘wrongs’.”

questions.q: What is “plastic” religiosity, as the article describes it?
options: Religion that changes from place to place
Not quite. The article says: Outward religious form without fear of God and real concern for others.
Religion learnt from books and not teachers
Not quite. The article says: Outward religious form without fear of God and real concern for others.
Religion practised with modern technology
Not quite. The article says: Outward religious form without fear of God and real concern for others.
Outward religious form without fear of God and real concern for others
Yes. It looks grand but has no fragrance.
questions.rationale: “If you examine them closely they have none of the true essence of religion, which is, fear of God and genuine concern for other human beings.”

questions.q: Three companions vowed to pray all night, fast every day and never marry. What did the Prophet’s reply teach?
options: Vows once made must be kept
Not quite. The article says: The spirit and quality of worship matter more than quantity; extremes are not his way.
More worship always brings more reward
Not quite. The article says: The spirit and quality of worship matter more than quantity; extremes are not his way.
The spirit and quality of worship matter more than quantity; extremes are not his way
Exactly. He prayed and slept, fasted and ate, and was married.
Only prophets may worship at night
Not quite. The article says: The spirit and quality of worship matter more than quantity; extremes are not his way.
questions.rationale: “It is the quality of our worship that is important, far more than the quantity… Extremism in deeds is against all practical wisdom.”

questions.q: What is the original and primary meaning of jihad, according to the article?
options: Striving hard to obey God – above all against one’s own desires and ego
Right. The Arabic word for war is qital.
Armed war against unbelievers
Not quite. The article says: Striving hard to obey God – above all against one’s own desires and ego.
Any act done in anger for religion
Not quite. The article says: Striving hard to obey God – above all against one’s own desires and ego.
The conquest of new lands
Not quite. The article says: Striving hard to obey God – above all against one’s own desires and ego.
questions.rationale: “The original meaning of jihad is striving very hard… the actual word for such a war in Arabic is qital, not jihad.”

questions.q: When a large force marched on Medina, the Prophet had a trench dug. What does the article see in this?
options: A deliberate choice to avoid battle, in keeping with his preference for the peaceful course
Yes. The same choice appears at Hudaybiya and at Makkah.
A plan to trap and destroy the enemy
Not quite. The article says: A deliberate choice to avoid battle, in keeping with his preference for the peaceful course.
A sign that the Muslims had no weapons
Not quite. The article says: A deliberate choice to avoid battle, in keeping with his preference for the peaceful course.
A custom borrowed to please the Quraysh
Not quite. The article says: A deliberate choice to avoid battle, in keeping with his preference for the peaceful course.
questions.rationale: “The digging of this trench provides an example of opting for a peaceful course instead of a violent course.”

questions.q: What should a person do at the moment of anger, according to the article?
options: Stay quiet and calm down before dealing with the matter
Correct. Rage is like a fire that dies for lack of fuel.
Say at once what he feels
Not quite. The article says: Stay quiet and calm down before dealing with the matter.
Seek out who was at fault
Not quite. The article says: Stay quiet and calm down before dealing with the matter.
Leave the relationship
Not quite. The article says: Stay quiet and calm down before dealing with the matter.
questions.rationale: “When we are angry, we should remain quiet, and try to calm ourselves before returning to dealing with the issue.”

questions.article: Prophet of Peace, or of Violence
questions.q: Ali named a newborn son Harab (“war”), and the Prophet asked him to change the name to Hasan (“goodness”). What does the article take from this?
options: Ali had wanted his son to be a soldier
Not quite. The article says: The Prophet’s love of peace was such that he did not like even a name that suggested violence.
The Prophet’s love of peace was such that he did not like even a name that suggested violence
Well read. He wished to cultivate a peaceful character.
Names decide a person’s fate
Not quite. The article says: The Prophet’s love of peace was such that he did not like even a name that suggested violence.
The Prophet chose the names of all children in Medina
Not quite. The article says: The Prophet’s love of peace was such that he did not like even a name that suggested violence.
questions.rationale: “His peace-loving nature was so heightened that he did not even like to hear the word Harab which had connotations of violence.”

questions.q: The Prophet stood up as a funeral passed. Told that the dead man was a Jew, what did he reply?
options: “It is the custom of this city.”
Not quite. The article says: “Was he not a human being?”.
“Was he not a human being?”
Yes. He saw every person first as a human being.
“He was our neighbour.”
Not quite. The article says: “Was he not a human being?”.
“I did not know.”
Not quite. The article says: “Was he not a human being?”.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet replied: ‘Was he not a human being?’ This ‘humanitarian’ outlook was typical of the Prophet’s vision of life.”
